claims.wording: iBoostUp is offered by iBoostUp Pty Ltd, an Australian registered company founded in 2010.

claims.conditions: Company registration not independently audited; use attribution.

claims.wording: The direct Mac download page advertises version 26.11, released 19 October 2026, macOS 10.11+ and native Apple Silicon support.
claims.excerpt: Version: 26.11 / Released: 19 Oct, 2026 / Supports macOS 10.11+ / Natively supports Apple Silicon Processors.
claims.conditions: Quoted segments separated by slashes; not installer inspection. FAQ legacy section separately directs 10.10/10.11 users to a legacy build; compatibility conflict must be disclosed, not resolved by assumption. Exact Intel architecture support not independently established.

claims.wording: Quick Clean is advertised free; optional features can be purchased in-app.
claims.excerpt: iBoostUp is completely free to download & use. Optional features can be purchased in-app. / iBoostUp's Quick Clean has always been legitimately free!
claims.conditions: Do not call every module free. Exact current optional-feature prices, periods, device counts, tax and renewal amounts unverified; no checkout opened.

claims.wording: iBoostUp documents a Disk Usage view with optional removal and a Quick Clean workflow for temporary files.
claims.excerpt: Disk Usage allows you to easily discover what's taking up space on your Mac, you can optionally remove these files and folders to regain disk space.
claims.conditions: Not a measured recovery result or safety certification; no app execution.

claims.wording: The FAQ describes reviewing Quick Clean results via More Information and says Duplicate File Finder removals can be recovered from Trash.
claims.excerpt: you are given the opportunity to review files detected for removal by clicking "More Information" on the results screen. / If you've inadvertently removed a file using Duplicate File Finder you can simply recover it from the Trash.
claims.conditions: Do not generalize Duplicate Finder Trash behavior to every cleaner. FAQ acknowledges files stored in temporary/system-cache locations may be removed.

claims.wording: Direct-download and App Store paid purchases do not interoperate; the App Store edition is sandboxed and asks for access before a scan.
claims.excerpt: if you install from the App Store it won't recognize your previous purchase from www.iboostup.com and vice versa / the App Store version of iBoostUp is sandboxed and prompts you for access before running a scan.
claims.conditions: Channel feature parity not established. Do not move licence entitlements between stores.

claims.wording: Spyware Doctor uses cloud logic; the FAQ says app file metadata is sent to its cloud.
claims.excerpt: We do this by a combination of heuristics, traditional signature scanning and logic deployed to the cloud. / we only ever send app file metadata to the Spyware Doctor cloud.
claims.conditions: Vendor description, not traffic/privacy audit. Never call entire suite offline. Privacy policy content inaccessible in this job.

claims.wording: The published EULA is a proprietary licence, not an open-source grant.

claims.conditions: Summarizes licence character only, not legal advice. Download-package redistribution provision is not screenshot republication permission.

workflowArticleBrief.primaryIntent: Decide which iBoostUp distribution to use and how to review a cleanup without confusing channel permissions, licence restoration and file recovery.
workflowArticleBrief.title: Before an iBoostUp cleanup: check the edition and review the files
workflowArticleBrief.description: Check iBoostUp's download channel, scan permissions and file-review options before cleanup. Its two Mac editions do not share paid purchases, and recovery differs by tool.
workflowArticleBrief.distinctValue: Channel-aware decision checklist, not a generic alternative list or expanded feature table.
outline: Choose the download channel before relying on an existing purchase (I06)
Separate Disk Usage inspection from Quick Clean removal (I03-I05)
Review the file list; do not extend Duplicate Finder Trash recovery to every module (I05)
Treat cloud-backed security separately from disk cleanup (I07)
When ongoing storage investigation fits better: one disclosed Breathing Room recommendation with preview/runtime/hosted caveats (B01-B03)
workflowArticleBrief.interactionPass: Handoff a non-mutating checklist: existing paid purchase channel -> same channel; need only inspect -> Disk Usage; considering removal -> review exact files and backup/rebuild consequences. No cleanup execution, login, cookies or upload required.
workflowArticleBrief.visualPlan: After lead: official iBoostUp Disk Usage app screenshot only once cleared. Later: selected Breathing Room Space example preview with full disclosure. No generated app UI.
workflowArticleBrief.scope: Documented workflow, not hands-on tutorial. Verify any extra macOS/backup advice against Apple sources during drafting. No terminal cleanup commands.

comparisonBrief.title: Breathing Room vs iBoostUp: storage investigation or a utility suite
comparisonBrief.primaryIntent: Choose a Mac storage/maintenance approach, not compare untested speed or savings.
comparisonBrief.lead: iBoostUp documents free Quick Clean and a broader utility catalogue; Breathing Room, which we build, focuses on storage investigation and app/activity context in a maintenance preview. Neither documentation set proves superior safety or measured performance.
iboostupAdvantages: Documented Duplicate Finder, cookie manager and uninstaller catalogue; do not claim equivalent Breathing Room tools or all-free access (S1)
Separate direct/App Store choice documented with concrete permission/licence caveats (I06)
